subject: Re: Q3 2028 Renewal — HyperMart bakeoff, dedicated uplift & term bridge
messages:
From: Ari Johnson <ari@hypermart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@hypermart.com>, procurement@hypermart.com
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion & bakeoff window request

Marcus —

We’re approaching our renewal for Q3 and the internal platform team has flagged a couple of things that could push us to evaluate alternatives:

- Recent throughput regressions on our peak pipelines (weekend loads) — we still see a 2–3x variance vs last year.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens is up ~18% compared to prior term.

There’s some internal momentum to run a bakeoff against QuickServe AI next month. Before we go that route we wanted to check whether Redwood can propose a short remediation and a commercial bridge that would make staying attractive.

Specifically, we need:
1) A reproducible benchmark plan we can run against our traffic (DevOps will run).
2) A concrete term/price proposal if performance is demonstrably improved.
3) Any temporary capacity uplift options while we validate.

Can you share a benchmark harness and an initial commercial bridge we can review? Procurement is expecting a note by next Friday.

Thanks —
Ari Johnson
Head of Platform, HyperMart
ari@hypermart.com

[Attachment: hypermart-procurement-checklist.xlsx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ari Johnson <ari@hypermart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion & bakeoff window request

Ari —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sharing the checklist. I’m sorry to hear you’ve had variance on peak loads — we take that very seriously. We’ll move fast on two parallel tracks: a technical benchmark window and a commercial bridge you can take to procurement.

Proposed next steps (high level):
- We’ll ship a small benchmark harness + instructions (attached) for your DevOps to run against a short sample of production traffic. 48–72 hour run recommended.
- Offer a 2-week dedicated uplift (isolated GPU pool) for the benchmark and pilot; no charge for the first week if results meet the SLO targets.
- Draft SLA amendment and a term bridge: 3-month capacity uplift at a "-20% list" pilot credit in exchange for committing to a 12-month extension if SLOs are met.

We’ve attached the benchmark-instructions.docx and a draft SLA amendment for your legal team to review. If you’re open, let’s lock the benchmark window for the week of May 6 so we can get results back before your procurement deadline.

Questions for you / ask to DevOps:
- Can you run the harness on your 95th percentile request shape?
- Do you have an embargoed endpoint to avoid mixing traffic?

I’ll loop in product ops and pricing to firm this up.

—Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0164

[Attachments: benchmark-instructions.docx, SLA_amendment_draft.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Renewal discussion & bakeoff window request

Marcus — forwarding Ari's ask and your proposed approach. High level ask from me: pricing / credit math and operational runway. Key points to evaluate before we hand a '-20% list' offer:

- How constrained is capacity in our Palo Alto pool the week of May 6? Can we guarantee isolation?
- If we offer guilt-free rollback, what are expected revenue and capacity impacts?
- Will procurement insist on a formal benchmark runbook (they almost always do) — checklist attached from Ari looks like the start of that.

Neha / Ben — please weigh in with pricing and legal guardrails. I want to avoid over-indexing on blunt discounts without operational commitments (e.g., burst window length, KB caching rules, model variant).

Marissa
Sr. Director, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Renewal discussion & bakeoff window request

Quick pricing thinking — all figures illustrative until Ben gives legal sign-off: 

- Baseline: current list = $0.45 / 1k tokens; effective HyperMart blended = $0.37 / 1k.
- Pilot offer: dedicated uplift for benchmark week — list rate charged but 100% credit applied for week 1 if 95th percentile latency and throughput targets are met.
- Bridge: 3-month uplift period at 20% off list (i.e., $0.36 / 1k) if they sign a 12-month extension within 30 days of successful benchmark.
- Safety net: automatic rollback clause — if SLOs missed on average for two consecutive weeks post-rollout, we revert pricing to prior effective rate for one billing cycle and issue a 15% service credit.

Operational asks for the product team:
- We should propose a quantized model variant (lower memory, better latency) for peak traffic as part of the pilot.
- Log-level KPIs to capture during the benchmark: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, cache hit ratio, and failed requests.

I can draft the credit math and a short term sheet. Marcus — can you confirm timeline with Ari?

—Neha
VP, Revenue Operations
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Renewal discussion & bakeoff window request

Looping in legal counsel notes — redline highlights of the SLA amendment: 

- Add explicit rollback and credit mechanics (Neha’s wording is fine but legal wants exact thresholds).
- Limit the pilot uplift to a maximum of 3 nodes / 24 GPUs in our dedicated pool; any additional capacity billed at standard committed-rate uplift.
- Require a signed bench-run statement from HyperMart certifying traffic sample authenticity (to avoid synthetic skew).
- Add a non-disparagement clause for the 90 days post-benchmark to prevent premature public bakeoff claims while we're resolving results.

I attached a short summary of suggested redlines (will send full tracked doc via DocuSign when we finalize). Recommend offering the pilot with the 1-week free credit and a 3-month -20% bridge but only if product ops signs off on the quantized variant viability.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[Attachment: SLA_amendment_redline_summary.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ari Johnson <ari@hypermart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@hypermart.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final pilot & term bridge proposal — HyperMart renewal

Ari —

Thanks again for working through the details with us. Based on the benchmark runbook we circulated and internal sign-offs, here is our formal offer to keep HyperMart on Redwood and to address the performance/cost concerns you raised: 

Summary offer (high level):
- Pilot: 2-week dedicated uplift for benchmarking and verification (isolated Palo Alto pool).
  - Week 1: free credit if 95th percentile latency and throughput targets are met.
  - Week 2: transitional billing at 20% off list.
- Bridge: if pilot meets the agreed KPIs, HyperMart signs a 12-month extension and receives a 3-month committed uplift at 20% off list (applied to uplift capacity only).
- SLA: draft amendment attached (SLA_amendment_draft.pdf) includes rollback mechanics and a 15% credit for sustained SLO misses as discussed.
- Legal / Operational guardrails: limited to 24 GPUs during the pilot unless HyperMart explicitly requests and pays for extra capacity; we’ll require a bench-run attestation from your DevOps team.

Attachments: SLA_amendment_draft.pdf, term_sheet_hypermart_v1.pdf, benchmark-instructions.docx

If this framework looks acceptable I’ll arrange the uplift for the week of June 3 and push the term sheet to procurement for signature. We’d like a signed DocuSign by June 14 to keep the bridge timings intact.

Open questions we still have:
- DevOps: can you confirm the sample window and provide the endpoint (or confirm a replayable capture) so we can schedule our engineers?
- Procurement: will HyperMart accept the attestation requirement?

Happy to jump on a 30 minute call tomorrow to walk through any of the items.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0164
